desc:
Given a string s of lowercase letters, find the longest substring in which each of the five vowels a, e, i, o, u appears an even number of times (zero counts as even). Return its length.

The empty substring always qualifies, so the answer is never negative. For example, in "bcbcbc" there are no vowels at all, so the answer is 6; in "aeiou" the best substring is empty, so the answer is 0; in "aabeb" the answer is 3 ("aab").
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Trying every substring and counting its vowels is O(n²). Think about prefixes instead of substrings.
Only the parity (odd or even) of each vowel count matters, so the state of a prefix fits in 5 bits.

A substring has all-even counts exactly when the prefix before it and the prefix at its end have the same parity mask. Store the first index at which each of the 32 masks appears, and at every position look up the current mask.
editorial: Let mask(i) be a 5-bit number whose bit v is 1 when the vowel v has appeared an odd number of times in s[0..i). The substring s[i..j) has all-even vowel counts exactly when mask(i) == mask(j), because XOR-ing two equal masks gives zero.

So, scanning left to right, we maintain the running mask and a table first[mask] with the earliest prefix length at which each mask was seen (the empty prefix has mask 0 at length 0). At prefix length j with mask m, if m was seen before at length i, the substring has length j - i; otherwise record j. The answer is the maximum. This is O(n) time and O(32) space.
